stages.reference: Create a subtle material study of the fine irregularities that belong to the established cobalt-blue stained glass. Within the same deep but translucent blue body, reveal a few delicate cooling ripples, almost hidden air inclusions and minor time-worn abrasion. Their edges should fade softly through the glass instead of reading as separately painted symbols. Keep the blue balanced, neither cyan nor violet, and avoid bright white glints that would force an artificially sharp finish. This is a detail layer: it must complement the corresponding blue glass, preserving unused transparency and source-defined coverage during later application. Avoid new panel geometry, ornamental leadwork, atmospheric cloud designs, intense reflections, large bubbles, deep cracks or opaque blue backgrounds.
